small_guidance:
- The bias_tanh epilogue is already memory-bound and tiny relative to the conv; further tuning of BLOCK/num_warps here won't move fast_p. If kept, try BLOCK=4096 with num_warps=4 and collapse (N,C,HW) into a 1D grid so launch overhead drops, but expected gain is <1%.
- Avoid the extra `x.contiguous()` call — ConvTranspose2d output is already contiguous; the redundant call may allocate/copy. Pass `x` directly.
- Use `tl.tanh(y)` directly instead of manual exp formulation to reduce register pressure (and on Ampere it maps to the hardware tanh approximation).
large_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose2d dominates runtime (~18.8 ms baseline vs 20.6 ms custom). Replace it with a custom Triton kernel implemented as a scatter-add of `input × weight` outer products into the output grid, handling stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1 in the index math, and fuse bias subtraction + tanh in the epilogue before store.
- Alternative: implement as a gather-style direct kernel where each program computes a tile of output pixels (oc, oh, ow) by iterating over (ic, kh, kw) and reading from input position ((oh+pad-kh)/stride, (ow+pad-kw)/stride) only when divisible by stride. Use channels_last layout so IC is the GEMM-K contiguous axis. Tile (BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SP=64, BLOCK_IC=32) with autotune; fuse the bias and tanh into the accumulator epilogue.
- Persist weights in shared memory across the IC reduction (kernel is only 64×64×4×4 = 64KB fp32 — half-precision cast or split-K may help). Avoid the standalone epilogue kernel entirely — the second full read/write of a 32×64×512×512 tensor is ~2 GB of traffic that the fused conv can eliminate.
